message: Affected versions of sharp are vulnerable to Divide By Zero / Heap-based Buffer Overflow / Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. sharp bundles a vulnerable version of the native libheif library, inheriting two critical memory-safety flaws in derived-item (`iden`) and auxiliary-item (`auxl`) handling: a heap buffer overflow in `scale_nearest_neighbor()` where duplicate alpha planes let a 10/12-bit sample be written into an 8-bit plane allocation with an attacker-controlled overflow size and contents (CVE-2026-84383), and a class of out-of-bounds reads and writes across roughly a dozen pixel-plane consumers that assume a `HeifPixelImage` logical geometry matching every channel plane it holds (GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545, for which a working code-execution exploit was confirmed). Decoding a crafted AVIF or HEIF image can therefore corrupt the heap and lead to remote code execution. Because sharp selects the libvips loader by sniffing the input bytes, no call site can be shown to be safe: `sharp(untrustedBuffer)` reaches the libheif loader exactly as `sharp("photo.avif")` does, and even a metadata-only `.metadata()` call parses the container. Upgrade to sharp 0.35.4 or later, which bundles libheif 1.23.2; if you rely on a globally-installed libvips, upgrade that libheif to 1.23.2. Blocking the HEIF-family loader with `sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadHeif"] })` is the only workaround that prevents the vulnerable decode path from being reached; running a `node` binary compiled as a Position Independent Executable merely blunts escalation to code execution and does not stop the heap corruption, and the official Node.js builds are not PIE. The heap corruption itself is platform-independent; the advisory documents escalation to remote code execution on glibc-based Linux hosts running a non-PIE `node` binary, so a finding on macOS or musl still represents an exploitable memory-safety bug.
